# 2 Baruch Chapter 44 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** Third Fast and Vision

---

**44:1** And I, Baruch, answered and said to the elders:

**44:2** Hear me, all you elders; and give ear, all you who are gathered here:

**44:3** You know that our fathers in times past forsook the law; and on account of this, evil things came upon them and upon us.

**44:4** But the hope of those who have kept the commandments of the Mighty One will not fail; and their portion will remain when the times have passed away.

**44:5** For the time of this world will pass away, and its glory will grow old, and all its beauty will decay; and the proud will be as though they had never been.

**44:6** And those who trust in wealth will be like those who have passed away; and those who exercise dominion over others will wail and be put to shame.

**44:7** For the things that are to come are of great worth and great excellence, while the things that are passing away are small and fleeting.

**44:8** All those therefore who have hoped in the Anointed One who was to come — all those will be in gladness; and those who were not in the number of the people of knowledge will be destroyed.

**44:9** For the hope of those who trusted in the law with their whole heart will not perish; it will not fail.

**44:10** And this lamp of the world — how long will it shine? And when will its darkness be destroyed, which at present covers everything?

**44:11** And for what reason does the beauty of the earth grow old? And for what reason will its strength be corrupted? And when will the Mighty One himself come in glory to judge all who dwell upon the earth?

---

*SOPHIA notes: Consensus rendering. Key decisions: "people of knowledge" (v.8) retained over PNEUMA's "people who truly know God" — the Syriac 'ida'ta is more neutral; "the lamp of this world" (v.10) follows LOGOS structure; all three converge on "the Anointed One who was to come" (v.8) as the messianic title.*
